messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Gabapentin is available as capsules, tablets, extended-release tablets, and an oral solution.
Strengths vary by product.
Different products are not interchangeable.
Neurontin and generic gabapentin
oral capsules 100 mg, 300 mg, 400 mg
oral tablets 600 mg, 800 mg
oral solution 250 mg/5 mL
Relgaabi
oral capsules 100 mg, 200 mg, 300 mg, 400 mg
Gralise
extended-release tablets 300 mg, 450 mg, 600 mg, 750 mg, and 900 mg
Horizant (gabapentin enacarbil)
extended-release tablets 300 mg, 600 mg
Note: The Horizant strengths refer to gabapentin enacarbil.
The Horizant strengths do not refer to gabapentin itself.
Therefore, Horizant doses do not correspond milligram-for-milligram to other gabapentin products.
Triplet: ["Horizant", "has active ingredient", "gabapentin enacarbil"]

The relation 'has active ingredient' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug contains the active pharmaceutical ingredient specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'contains ingredient': The subject drug product contains the active ingredient specified by the object entity.
B. 'has dosage form': The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
C. 'may be used for': The subject drug may be used for the purpose or condition specified by the object entity.
D. 'has status': The subject drug has a specific status or classification specified by the object entity.
E. 'manufactured by': The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.
